Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- An Archivist who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the archive op, which spends the token; code shows them the drawn roles at once, as a night result. Don't tell() the Archivist anything about it.
- Track Arsonist douses with set_status key 'doused' value true. An ignite uses up every douse: clear 'doused' on everyone it hit, survivors included (rules: Arsonist). Don't tell anyone they were doused: code tells the doused players who should know.
- A Census Taker who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the census op; code draws the group and the count and tells them. Don't tell() the Census Taker anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- A Chronicler who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the mark op, which spends the token; code sets the mark; when the marked player dies, the death announcement reveals their role unless a Mortician cleans them. Don't tell() the Chronicler anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. The mark lasts for the rest of the game, even after the Chronicler dies. Don't tell the marked player.
- A Diviner who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the divine op; code draws the role and tells them. Don't tell() the Diviner anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. If they picked a Yakuza, don't use the op: that player has Strong Defense tonight, and the Diviner gets no result.
- Executioner revenge attacks are carried out by code after you finish; don't resolve them. Code also turns an Executioner whose target died tonight into a Jester at dawn: don't set any status for it.
- Tell the Fortune Teller their two numbers about tonight's visits now, as a night result, each labeled (e.g. '4 players were visited; 3 players visited someone'). Self-visits count in both numbers, and a player who visits several players (e.g. a Katana holder also using their own action) counts once as a visitor. A role-block doesn't stop it (R9): tell them even if they were blocked.
- Ritualist who spent tokens (and wasn't role-blocked): compare the guessed role with the target's exact role (a Roleplayer is a Roleplayer). Right: deal the Attack (1 token Standard, 2 Divine). Wrong: no Attack; announce it with tell(['all'], '<name> is a Ritualist.') tonight, which is read out at the start of the next Day, even if the Ritualist dies tonight. Astral Visit.
- Code tells the Scout their result every night from your record_visits list; don't tell() them anything about it.
- The Seer learns about two random players other than themself each night (random_choice) from those alive when the night began, including anyone who died that night (rules R10), unless they spent a token to choose them. A chosen pair visits both players; the random pair isn't a visit. A role-blocked Seer gets no pair at all.
- A Talent Agent who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the scout_talent op, with role set to the role they named (guessed_role) to count it, or without role to scan; it spends the token, and at most one a night. Code tells them the result: don't tell() the Talent Agent anything about it. It targets no player, so it visits no one.
- Trapper: traps persist across nights and code keeps them. For each Trapper who acted (and wasn't role-blocked), use the set_trap op before any spring_trap: player = where its trap goes, or null if it acted with no target (that removes its trap). A new trap replaces its old one at once, so the old one doesn't act tonight. Trapping the player its trap is already on isn't allowed (the trap stays): code refuses it. A trap is armed from the night after it's placed (trapped_by status lists the traps on a player). If anyone made a non-Divine Attack on a player with an armed trap tonight, use the spring_trap op once for that player with every such attack still standing, each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral or not a visit, e.g. a Veteran's alert or a trap's hit-back)}. Resolve it right after any protection that acts before all others (a fox charm: leave out the attack it swallowed) and before Defense (Medic, ...). Code has every armed trap on that player act in random order, each stopping a different attack, and uses them up: treat each stopped attack as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), and code says whether each trap hits its attacker back. Code tells the Trappers their results; don't tell() them about traps.
- Armed (a trait, R24): a player whose trait_actions has trait 'Armed' fires their one hidden-gun shot at its target, in addition to their role's action. It is an action and a visit (R6; record it, and an alerting Veteran's attack hits the shooter): a role-block stops it along with their role's action, and then the shot isn't used. Unless they were role-blocked, use the fire_gun op (it marks the shot used, even if the attack fails) and resolve a Basic Attack on the target (R3): a kill's cause is 'a hidden gun' and its by is the shooter. Tell the shooter only whether their shot killed its target, never the target's role, and tell a surviving target they were attacked.
- Sleepwalker (a trait, R24): code draws each Sleepwalker's random visit; it is in their trait_actions as {trait: 'Sleepwalker', target, automatic: true}. It is a visit (R6): record it with record_visits, and anything that sees or reacts to visits (Tracker, Lookout, Veteran, traps) counts it. It does nothing else. A role-block stops it (no visit). Never tell the Sleepwalker whom they visited.
- Disguised (a trait, R24): every exact-role check (R18: e.g. an Oracle's or Ritualist's guess, a Mortician's clean) sees these players as these Village roles, alive or dead: Bob as Enforcer; Carol as Prosecutor. Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trapper'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- An Archivist who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the archive op, which spends the token; code shows them the drawn roles at once, as a night result. Don't tell() the Archivist anything about it.
- Track Arsonist douses with set_status key 'doused' value true. An ignite uses up every douse: clear 'doused' on everyone it hit, survivors included (rules: Arsonist). Don't tell anyone they were doused: code tells the doused players who should know.
- A Census Taker who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the census op; code draws the group and the count and tells them. Don't tell() the Census Taker anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- A Chronicler who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the mark op, which spends the token; code sets the mark; when the marked player dies, the death announcement reveals their role unless a Mortician cleans them. Don't tell() the Chronicler anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. The mark lasts for the rest of the game, even after the Chronicler dies. Don't tell the marked player.
- A Diviner who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the divine op; code draws the role and tells them. Don't tell() the Diviner anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. If they picked a Yakuza, don't use the op: that player has Strong Defense tonight, and the Diviner gets no result.
- Executioner revenge attacks are carried out by code after you finish; don't resolve them. Code also turns an Executioner whose target died tonight into a Jester at dawn: don't set any status for it.
- Tell the Fortune Teller their two numbers about tonight's visits now, as a night result, each labeled (e.g. '4 players were visited; 3 players visited someone'). Self-visits count in both numbers, and a player who visits several players (e.g. a Katana holder also using their own action) counts once as a visitor. A role-block doesn't stop it (R9): tell them even if they were blocked.
- Ritualist who spent tokens (and wasn't role-blocked): compare the guessed role with the target's exact role (a Roleplayer is a Roleplayer). Right: deal the Attack (1 token Standard, 2 Divine). Wrong: no Attack; announce it with tell(['all'], '<name> is a Ritualist.') tonight, which is read out at the start of the next Day, even if the Ritualist dies tonight. Astral Visit.
- Code tells the Scout their result every night from your record_visits list; don't tell() them anything about it.
- The Seer learns about two random players other than themself each night (random_choice) from those alive when the night began, including anyone who died that night (rules R10), unless they spent a token to choose them. A chosen pair visits both players; the random pair isn't a visit. A role-blocked Seer gets no pair at all.
- A Talent Agent who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the scout_talent op, with role set to the role they named (guessed_role) to count it, or without role to scan; it spends the token, and at most one a night. Code tells them the result: don't tell() the Talent Agent anything about it. It targets no player, so it visits no one.
- Trapper: traps persist across nights and code keeps them. For each Trapper who acted (and wasn't role-blocked), use the set_trap op before any spring_trap: player = where its trap goes, or null if it acted with no target (that removes its trap). A new trap replaces its old one at once, so the old one doesn't act tonight. Trapping the player its trap is already on isn't allowed (the trap stays): code refuses it. A trap is armed from the night after it's placed (trapped_by status lists the traps on a player). If anyone made a non-Divine Attack on a player with an armed trap tonight, use the spring_trap op once for that player with every such attack still standing, each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral or not a visit, e.g. a Veteran's alert or a trap's hit-back)}. Resolve it right after any protection that acts before all others (a fox charm: leave out the attack it swallowed) and before Defense (Medic, ...). Code has every armed trap on that player act in random order, each stopping a different attack, and uses them up: treat each stopped attack as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), and code says whether each trap hits its attacker back. Code tells the Trappers their results; don't tell() them about traps.
- Armed (a trait, R24): a player whose trait_actions has trait 'Armed' fires their one hidden-gun shot at its target, in addition to their role's action. It is an action and a visit (R6; record it, and an alerting Veteran's attack hits the shooter): a role-block stops it along with their role's action, and then the shot isn't used. Unless they were role-blocked, use the fire_gun op (it marks the shot used, even if the attack fails) and resolve a Basic Attack on the target (R3): a kill's cause is 'a hidden gun' and its by is the shooter. Tell the shooter only whether their shot killed its target, never the target's role, and tell a surviving target they were attacked.
- Sleepwalker (a trait, R24): code draws each Sleepwalker's random visit; it is in their trait_actions as {trait: 'Sleepwalker', target, automatic: true}. It is a visit (R6): record it with record_visits, and anything that sees or reacts to visits (Tracker, Lookout, Veteran, traps) counts it. It does nothing else. A role-block stops it (no visit). Never tell the Sleepwalker whom they visited.
- Disguised (a trait, R24): every exact-role check (R18: e.g. an Oracle's or Ritualist's guess, a Mortician's clean) sees these players as these Village roles, alive or dead: Bob as Enforcer; Carol as Prosecutor.
